P14 saving two-stage shrink STAGE ORDER: pre-2021 CV (saving 2017->2021, persistence base) prefers the incumbent region->income-group (6.505) over the challenger income->region (6.511) by a razor-thin 0.006pp — CV-adoption condition fails at the first gate, so the incumbent order stays; out-of-sample predictions byte-identical to P13 champion (account 5.105 / resilience 6.625 / saving 7.359); stage order is practically irrelevant for stacked orthogonal-basin shrinkage (the two basins nearly commute); reverted predictor.py to P13 champion (1bda919)

P16 THIRD-stage shrinkage for saving with a data-driven basin (terciles of the account level = 'digitalization stage'), stacked on the P12 damped trend + region -> income-group shrink, k=0.1 each: pre-2021 CV (saving 2017->2021, persistence base, all basins built at 2017) prefers three-stage (6.408) over two-stage (6.505); out-of-sample saving MAE 7.359->7.080 (-0.279pp); account (5.105) and resilience (6.625) byte-identical to the P13 champion; orthogonal-basin shrinkage compounds a third time and a DATA-DRIVEN basin works alongside the geographic/administrative ones - noise correction keeps transferring across the 2021 regime change where dynamics-tuning (P9/P10) and cross-indicator fits (P15) did not

P17 THIRD-stage shrinkage for ACCOUNT with a data-driven CROSS-INDICATOR basin (terciles of the g20_any digital-payment level), stacked on the P13 income-group -> region shrink, k=0.1 each: pre-2021 CV (account 2017->2021, persistence base, all basins built at 2017) prefers three-stage (6.710) over two-stage (6.958) by a comfortable margin; out-of-sample account MAE 5.105->5.014 (-0.091pp); saving (7.080) and resilience (6.625) byte-identical to the P16 champion. The data-driven third stage GENERALIZES to a second target, and notably its gain (-0.091pp) is LARGER than account's second administrative stage bought (-0.039pp) -- a basin drawn from a different indicator carries more independent signal than a second geographic/administrative cut. Orthogonal-basin noise correction remains the one mechanism transferring across the 2021 regime change (vs P9/P10 dynamics-tuning and P15 cross-indicator ridge, both non-transfers)

P18 FOURTH-stage shrinkage for saving with a SECOND cross-indicator data-driven basin (terciles of the g20_any digital-payment level), stacked on the P16 champion (damped trend + region -> income-group -> account-tercile shrink), k=0.1 at every stage: pre-2021 CV (saving 2017->2021, persistence base, all basins built at 2017) prefers four-stage (6.370) over three-stage (6.408); out-of-sample saving MAE 7.080->6.831 (-0.249pp); account (5.014) and resilience (6.625) byte-identical to the P17 champion. Compounding does NOT stop at three stages and is barely diminishing on this target (stage 3 bought -0.279pp, stage 4 -0.249pp), even though the two data-driven basins (account terciles, g20 terciles) are both digitalization cuts and might have been near-collinear. Orthogonal-basin noise correction remains the one mechanism transferring across the 2021 regime change (vs P9/P10 dynamics-tuning and P15 cross-indicator ridge)

P19 FOURTH-stage shrinkage for ACCOUNT with a second cross-indicator data-driven basin (terciles of fin17a_17a1_d, the formal-saving level), mirroring P18's saving design on the P17 champion (income-group -> region -> g20-tercile), k=0.1: the pre-2021 CV (account 2017->2021, persistence base, all basins built at 2017) REJECTS it decisively -- three_stage=6.710 vs four_stage=7.133 (+0.423pp worse), an order of magnitude past P14's razor-thin 0.006pp margin. Adoption condition fails at the first gate, so no 2024 evaluation was run (P14/P15 protocol) and predictor.py reverted to the P18 champion; all three MAEs byte-identical (account 5.014 / resilience 6.625 / saving 6.831). Answer to the registered question: the compounding curve IS target-specific -- saving took four stages, account stops at three.

P20 FIFTH-stage shrinkage for SAVING on a NON-digitalization data-driven basin (terciles of fin22a_22a1_22g_d, the formal-borrowing level), stacked on the P18 champion (damped trend + region -> income-group -> account-tercile -> g20-tercile), k=0.1: the pre-2021 CV (saving 2017->2021, persistence base, all basins built at 2017) REJECTS it -- four_stage=6.370 vs five_stage=6.644 (+0.274pp worse), 46x P14's razor-thin margin and of the same order as P19's account rejection (+0.423pp). Adoption fails at the first gate, so no 2024 evaluation was run (P14/P15/P19 protocol) and predictor.py reverted to the P18 champion; all three MAEs byte-identical (account 5.014 / resilience 6.625 / saving 6.831). Answer to the registered question: saving's compounding stops at four stages, and the basin material matters -- both basins that PAID for saving are digitalization cuts (account terciles -0.279pp, g20 terciles -0.249pp) while the first NON-digitalization basin tried is actively harmful. Orthogonality alone does not buy a stage; the partition has to track the phenomenon. Consistent with E11 (d_borrow ~ d_saving r=+0.403, the registered risk): borrowing LEVELS mis-partition saving levels even though borrowing CHANGES co-move with saving changes

P21 FOURTH-stage shrinkage for ACCOUNT on a DIGITALIZATION data-driven basin (terciles of fin32_acc, wage digitalization, 117/117 panel coverage at 2017/2021), stacked on the P17 champion (income-group -> region -> g20-tercile), k=0.1: registered to separate P19's 'target-specific curve' reading from P20's 'basin material' reading, because P19's rejected basin (formal-saving terciles) was a DEPTH indicator, not a digitalization cut. The pre-2021 CV (account 2017->2021, persistence base, all basins built at 2017) REJECTS it too: three_stage=6.710 vs four_stage=6.780 (+0.070pp worse). Adoption fails at the first gate, so no 2024 evaluation was run (P14/P15/P19/P20 protocol) and predictor.py reverted to the P18 champion; all three MAEs byte-identical (account 5.014 / resilience 6.625 / saving 6.831). Answer to the registered question: P19's reading SURVIVES -- account's compounding curve really is exhausted at three stages, and swapping in the best available digitalization basin does not revive it. But the margin is informative: 0.070pp here vs 0.423pp for the depth basin (P19) and 0.274pp for saving's borrowing basin (P20), i.e. basin material still modulates HOW BADLY a rejected stage hurts (a digitalization cut is near-neutral where non-digitalization cuts are clearly harmful) -- it just cannot buy a stage once the target's noise is gone. The two lessons are complementary, not competing: target-specific exhaustion (P19) sets WHETHER another stage is available, basin material (P20) sets how much a wrong stage costs
